problem: The symbol t appears in both crossing formulas without ever being defined, so a student cannot tell what it measures.
fix: Add before the formulas: t is the fraction of the way from P to Q along the edge, with t = 0 at P and t = 1 at Q; t = (k − Px) ÷ (Qx − Px) for a vertical boundary x = k.

where: Section 3, extra edges from concave polygons
problem: "Those edges have zero width" is not a correct description. The extra edges are ordinary line segments lying along the window boundary; what matters is that they enclose no area, so the filled region is unchanged.
fix: Say: those extra edges run along the window boundary and enclose no area, so they do not change the filled region; the scan-fill rules in Unit 1 fill the shape correctly.

problem: The trap says polygons that split into several separate outlines "need Weiler–Atherton", but Section 3 has just said a concave polygon that splits into separate visible pieces is handled by Sutherland–Hodgman with boundary connecting edges. The two statements contradict each other and the trap overstates the limitation.
fix: Say: Sutherland–Hodgman clips a single contour. It cannot represent holes, and when a concave polygon splits into separate pieces it joins them with degenerate edges along the window boundary. Weiler–Atherton avoids both problems and gives clean separate outlines, so use it for holes and for split results.
